questions.question: What is the main function of an introduction in a speech?
choices: Orient the audience, establish the topic, and preview the central idea

questions.question: Which organization best fits a speech explaining how a process works?
choices: Present steps in a logical sequence
Start with the conclusion and omit transitions

questions.question: A speaker cites a statistic but gives no source. What should be improved?
choices: Provide enough source information for the audience to evaluate it

questions.question: What is a useful role for a visual aid?
choices: Display every sentence the speaker will say
Clarify or emphasize information that is difficult to understand from words alone

questions.question: A speaker talks too quickly for the audience to follow. Which revision is most useful?
choices: Practice pacing and add purposeful pauses at key transitions
Raise the volume without changing pace

questions.question: Which opening is most likely to engage an audience while connecting to the topic?
choices: A brief relevant scenario or question that leads into the central idea

questions.question: Why should a speaker consider audience knowledge?
choices: It lets the speaker avoid evidence
It helps determine what needs explanation and which examples will be clear
It sets the speech's font size

questions.question: Which choice is the strongest thesis for a persuasive speech?
choices: The city should add protected bike lanes on two routes because safety data and ridership demand support them

questions.question: A presentation contains six slides of dense paragraphs. What is the best improvement?
choices: Reduce text and use concise points that support the spoken explanation
Shrink the font until everything fits

questions.question: What does a transition do in a speech?
choices: Shows how one point connects to the next

questions.question: A speaker's hands partly cover the projected chart. What should the speaker do?
choices: Add more text over the chart
Adjust position so the audience can see the visual

questions.question: Which practice improves vocal clarity?
choices: Speak in a monotone at any speed
Articulate words and vary emphasis to make key ideas understandable

questions.question: What belongs in a conclusion?
choices: A concise return to the central idea and a purposeful closing
A new major argument with no support
Every detail repeated word for word

questions.question: A student has five minutes for a talk and eight minutes of material. What should the student do?
choices: Prioritize the central claim and strongest supporting points
Skip the introduction and conclusion without planning

questions.question: Why rehearse with the actual slides or visual aids?
choices: To check timing, transitions, readability, and technical flow
To prove that no questions will arise

questions.question: Which visual is most useful for showing change over time?
During questions, a speaker does not know an answer. What is the most responsible response?
choices: Acknowledge the uncertainty and explain how the answer could be checked
Pretend the question was not asked

questions.question: How should a speaker handle a quotation on a slide?
choices: Attribute it and explain how it supports the point
Use it as a substitute for the entire argument

questions.question: A speaker notices the audience looks confused after a technical term. What is a useful response?
choices: Move to a more complex idea
Define the term with a brief example
Assume the audience is not listening

questions.question: Which rehearsal strategy best reduces dependence on reading a script word for word?
choices: Practice from an outline and key phrases while maintaining the intended structure
